key_concept: Each feature of a cloning vector or each step of rDNA technology has a specific role: ori controls replication, the cloning site is a restriction enzyme recognition site, selectable markers are usually antibiotic-resistance genes, and transformation introduces DNA into the host.
steps: A. Transformation is the procedure by which recombinant DNA is introduced into host bacterial cells, for example $Ca^{2+}$-treated competent E. coli followed by heat shock. So A matches II.
B. A cloning site is a unique recognition sequence where a restriction enzyme cuts the vector so the foreign DNA can be ligated in, for example the BamHI site in pBR322. So B matches I.
C. Selection separates transformants from non-transformants using selectable markers. These are usually antibiotic-resistance genes such as $amp^R$ and $tet^R$. So C matches IV.
D. Ori (origin of replication) is the sequence where replication starts. It also controls the copy number of the linked DNA. So D matches III.
The correct combination is A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III, which is option (1).
why_not_others: Option (2) wrongly links transformation to the restriction enzyme and the cloning site to DNA transfer. Options (3) and (4) mismatch ori, which controls replication and has nothing to do with restriction enzymes or DNA transfer.
common_trap: Students often link 'Transformation' to restriction enzymes because both are rDNA steps, forgetting that transformation means getting DNA into the host cell.
time_saving_tip: Ori–Replication is the surest pair (D-III). Only options (1) and (2) have it, and of these only option (1) pairs Transformation with transfer of DNA to host bacteria (A-II).
